title: CreaBIM model
description: A CreaBIM model described in JSON, format version 1. Lengths are in metres unless `units` says otherwise. See docs/json-format.md.

Model.description: A whole model: the file's top level. Every list may be left out. Ids are chosen by you, are unique across the whole file, and are what elements use to refer to each other (a door names its wall's id, a plan names its level's id).

$schema.description: Where an editor finds this schema; ignored by CreaBIM.

version.description: The format version the file is written to. This CreaBIM reads 1.

units.description: The unit every length in the file is in, except the sizes and positions on sheets, which are always paper millimetres. Angles are always degrees.

display_units.description: How the project shows and takes lengths (the model is metres whatever this says).

datum.description: The site datum: how high the project's zero stands above sea level, in metres whatever `units` says. Site levels are written above it.

assemblies.description: Layered build-ups for walls, floors and roofs.

types.description: Element types: wall types, door and window types, slab, roof, column and beam types.

openings.description: Doors, windows and bare holes, each in a wall.

parts.description: Extrusions and sweeps, solid or voids that cut what they meet.

objects.description: Furniture and fixtures from the catalogue.

tags.description: Tags of doors, windows, rooms and other elements, in views.

notes.description: Text written in a view or on a sheet.

LengthIn.description: A unit lengths are written in.

precision.description: Decimal places; for feet and inches, the smallest fraction of an inch as a power of two (3 is 1/8").

Material.description: What elements are made of: their colour in 3D and the hatch on their cut faces. Start from a library material by its name, or give the values yourself; any value given overrides the library's.

name.description: Shown in the app; the id when left out.

library.description: A material of CreaBIM's library, by name ("Concrete, cast in place"), to start from.

category.description: IFC's material category: concrete, brick, wood, steel, glass...

metallic.description: 0 for almost everything, 1 for bare metal.

rate.description: Its price for the take-off, in the project's currency, for each `rate_per`.

rate_per.description: What `rate` prices: square metres (the default), cubic metres, metres or pieces.

Hatch.description: The pattern on a material's cut faces.

RatePer.description: What a material's rate is priced per.

Assembly.description: A layered build-up. Walls list layers from the exterior face in; floors and roofs from the top down. An element built of one is as thick as its layers.

material.description: A material's id; none for an air gap.

priority.description: Which layer wins where walls join: 1 cuts through 5. Left out, it follows the layer's function (structure 1, finish 5).

LayerFunction.description: What a layer does. The core runs from the first structure layer to the last.

Type.description:
An element type: shared values its instances take, so editing the type in the app changes them all. An instance names it in its `type` field and may still set any of those values itself.

Which fields a category uses: wall: `thickness` (or `assembly`), `material`, `location`, `height`, `screen`; door and window: `width`, `height`, `sill`, `frame`, `material`; slab and roof: `thickness` (or `assembly`), `material`; column: `width` and `depth`, or `diameter`, and `material`; beam: `width`, `depth`, `material`.

boundary.description: With location `layer-boundary`: which boundary, counted from the exterior face (0) to the interior face (the layer count).

height.description: A wall type's height for new walls; a door or window's height.

screen.description: Makes a wall type a screen wall: a repeating unit with holes.

Location.description: The line a wall is drawn along and kept on when it gets thicker. The exterior is on the wall's right, looking from start to end, unless the wall is flipped.

Frame.description: How a door or window is built inside its opening: a frame round its outline, and inside it a grid of cells, each a fixed light or a panel that opens.

width.description: Face width of the frame members.

depth.description: Depth of the frame through the wall.

rise.description: A segmental arch's rise from its springing to its crown, or a raked head's fall from its start to its end (negative: it falls towards the start), in metres. Not used by the other outlines.

leaf.description: What a door's leaves are made as.

leaf_panes_across.description: A `french` or `slim-steel` leaf's panes across, each leaf (none: as `leaf_panes_up` says, or about 300 mm wide each, 400 for slim steel).

leaf_panes_up.description: Its panes up (none: about 360 mm high each, 450 for slim steel). Set both or neither.

lining.description: A lining board's thickness on the reveal, room side (0: none).

architrave.description: An architrave's face width round the opening, room side (0: none).

threshold.description: A threshold's height under a door (0: none).

acoustic_rating.description: Declared sound reduction, information only: "Rw 32 dB".

u_value.description: Declared thermal transmittance, W/m²K, information only.

accessible.description: Declared suitable for people with disabilities.

columns.description: The grid's columns from the opening's start (none: one).

rows.description: The grid's rows from the bottom (none: one).

cells.description: The cells, row by row from the bottom row, each row from the opening's start. None: a door's one hinged leaf or a window's one fixed light, or what `operation` describes.

operation.description: Before cells: how it opens, read only when `cells` is empty.

active_share.description: Before cells: a pair's active leaf share of the clear width.

panels.description: Before cells: a multi-panel slider's panels.

fixed.description: Before cells: a multi-panel slider's fixed panels, from 1.

panes_across.description: Before cells: window panes side by side.

panes_up.description: Before cells: window panes one above the other.

Outline.description: An opening's shape in its wall.

LeafStyle.description: What a door's leaves are made as.

GlassFittings.description: How an all glass leaf is held.

Track.description: A column or row of an opening's grid.

share.description: Its share of the clear width or height, relative to the others ([1, 1] splits it equally).

bar.description: A mullion or transom between it and the one before.

Cell.description: One cell of an opening's grid.

hand.description: Hinged (or sliding) towards the opening's end, not its start.

flipped.description: Opens to the other side from its opening's own: from the side a door opens to, or the outside a window faces.

active.description: Has the handle: the leaf opened first in a pair.

track.description: Which track a sliding panel runs on (0 or 1).

panes_across.description: Glass panes side by side, split by glazing bars.

panes_up.description: Glass panes one above the other.

across.description: How many columns it spans from its own, as a transom light over the whole opening; the places it covers are not cells of their own.

Operation.description: How a door or window opened before cells.

Screen.description: The repeating unit of a screen wall (breeze block, louvres, lattice).

unit.description: The unit's size, joints included: along the wall and up.

holes.description: The open rectangles of one unit, from its lower left corner.

frame.description: A solid border this wide round the screen.

stagger.description: Every other course shifted half a unit along.

Rect.description: A rectangle by its lower left and upper right corners.

Level.description: A storey. Elements hang off a level, so moving it moves them.

elevation.description: Height of its floor above the project's zero.

height.description: Floor-to-floor height: the height walls on it take unless told otherwise.

GridGroup.description: A grid system: how its lines are labelled and coloured.

prefix.description: Put before every label: "A-" gives A-1, A-2...

vertical.description: How lines running north-south are labelled, west to east.

horizontal.description: How lines running east-west are labelled, south to north.

label.description: Its label after its group's prefix; the id when left out.

Wall.description: A straight wall along its centreline on a level.

mark.description: Its mark, shown by tags and schedules; none numbers it automatically.

type.description: A wall type's id: the wall takes its thickness, assembly, material, location line and height.

thickness.description: Needed unless the wall has a type or an assembly.

height.description: Height above its base. Left out: up to `top_level` when given, else the type's height, else its level's height.

top_level.description: A level's id: the top stays `top_offset` above that level as levels move.

boundary.description: With location `layer-boundary`: which boundary, counted from the exterior face (0) to the interior face (the layer count).

flip.description: The exterior face on the left instead of the right.

attach_top.description: Roofs and slabs (ids) the top follows the underside of.

Opening.description: A door, window or bare hole in a wall, placed by its distance along the wall from the wall's start; or a roof window, placed in plan on its roof.

offset.description: From the wall's start to the opening's near edge. Give this or `centre`.

centre.description: From the wall's start to the opening's middle.

type.description: A door or window type's id: the opening takes its width, height, sill, frame and material.

width.description: Needed unless the opening has a type.

height.description: Needed unless the opening has a type.

sill.description: Its bottom above the wall's base. Left out: 0 for doors and holes, 0.9 m for windows (or the type's).

flip_hand.description: A door hinged on the jamb at the wall's end side.

flip_facing.description: A door opening to the wall's exterior; a window facing its interior.

roof_at.description: A roof window's centre in plan. With it, `wall` is the id of the roof the window is set in, its width runs across the slope and its height up it, and `offset`, `centre` and `sill` are not used.

arrangement.description: Windows that make one thing together: side by side in a ribbon, round a corner, in a bay or a bow. Left out: on its own.

Arrangement.description: How a window stands with others. Each keeps its own frame; the windows of one group share its number.

group.description: The group's number, the same for every window in it.

corner_start.description: Its end at the wall's start reaches into the corner there.

corner_end.description: Its end at the wall's end reaches into the corner there.

joint.description: How it meets the window round the corner.

left_start.description: At its start's corner the other wall runs off to this wall's left, else to its right.

left_end.description: The same at its end's corner.

angle_start.description: At its start's corner, the other wall's way off as an angle (radians) from this wall's direction towards its left.

angle_end.description: The same at its end's corner.

ArrangementKind.description: What a group of windows makes.

CornerJoint.description: Where two windows meet at a corner.

Slab.description: A floor slab: its outline pushed down from its top face.

outline.description: The corners in plan, either way round.

bulges.description: How each edge bends (corner i to i + 1): the tangent of a quarter of the arc's angle, positive bulging left. 0 or left out is straight.

holes.description: Holes through it, each an outline inside it.

thickness.description: Needed unless the slab has a type or an assembly.

top_offset.description: Its top face above its level; negative for below.

Roof.description: A roof over a wall-plate outline.

outline.description: Where the slopes start, in plan.

pitch.description: Slope in degrees. Needed unless the roof is flat.

overhang.description: How far it reaches past the outline, in plan.

thickness.description: Square to the slope. Needed unless the roof has a type or an assembly.

edge.description: The outline edge a shed roof rises from, or a gable roof's ridge runs along (edge i runs from corner i to i + 1).

holes.description: Holes cut upright through it (roof lights, a chimney).

Column.description: A column: a rectangular (`width` × `depth`) or round (`diameter`) profile standing on a level.

rotation.description: Turn of the profile, degrees anticlockwise.

height.description: A fixed height. Left out: up to `top_level`, else to the next level up.

Beam.description: A beam, its top `top_offset` below the top of its storey.

Stair.description: A stair: drawn by a line (its walk line or a side), with a landing at each corner; or, without a line, one flight or two with a landing between.

start.description: The middle of the first riser, in plan.

direction.description: Which way the first flight climbs, degrees anticlockwise from x.

max_riser.description: The tallest riser allowed; the risers share the height equally.

height.description: A fixed rise. Left out: up to the next level.

waist.description: Thickness of the sloping slab under the steps.

line.description: The line it was drawn by, in plan, from `start`. Its corners are landings.

bends.description: How far each straight of `line` bends into an arc: degrees its direction turns through, to the left when positive.

drawn.description: Which line of the stair `line` is.

flights.description: Flights given their own number of treads; the others take the rest.

landings.description: Landings made deeper than the line leaves them.

winders.description: How many winders at each turn (0: one for each 30° it turns).

build.description: How it is built: what carries its treads.

finish.description: What its treads, risers and landings are finished in.

rules.description: The rule set it is checked against: `comfort`, `ontario`, `us`, `uk`, or the name of one of the project's own.

ramp.description: A ramp, not steps: its steepest slope, rise over run (1:12 is 0.0833). A ramp's `tread` and `max_riser` follow from it.

typical.description: Stacked: the id of the stair at the foot of the stack this one repeats on a typical floor. It is kept the same as that stair.

split.description: A split stair: its line is one arm; the stair is that arm and its mirror image, sharing one flight twice as wide up to the first landing.

up_label.description: Where its UP label stands, moved from before its first flight: the offset in plan. Left out: before the flight.

Landing.description: A landing that turns a stair.

after.description: The number of risers before it.

StairLine.description: Which line of a stair it was drawn by.

StairFlight.description: A flight of a line stair given its own number of treads.

straight.description: The straight of the line it runs along, from 0.

StairLanding.description: A landing of a line stair made deeper: the flight before it stops this much sooner.

turn.description: The turn of the line it sits at, from 0.

StairTurnKind.description: What a turn of a stair becomes.

StairTurn.description: A turn of a line stair given its own kind.

turn.description: The turn of the line, from 0.

winders.description: How many winders (0: one for each 30° it turns).

StairFinish.description: The finishes over a stair's structure. Its risers are measured finish to finish; the structure sits the tread finish lower.

tread.description: The finish on each tread, landing and winder: its thickness.

riser.description: The finish on each riser's face (none where risers are open).

nosing.description: How far each tread's finish runs out past the riser below.

Railing.description: A railing along a path, or along one side of a stair.

path.description: Points of its path, heights above the level. Not used when it follows a stair.

stair.description: A stair's id: the railing follows its `side`.

extend.description: On a stair: how far the handrail runs on past its ends.

on_wall.description: A handrail on a wall: brackets, ends back to the wall.

infill.description: What fills a guard below its top rail.

guard_height.description: A guard taller than its handrail: its top rail's height; the handrail stays at `height` on its posts.

newels.description: Heavier posts at its ends and corners; a steep rail stops at one and starts again higher.

RailExtend.description: How a stair's handrail runs on past its bottom and top nosings.

slope_bottom.description: The rail keeps its slope for one going before running level.

RailInfill.description: What fills a guard below its top rail.

Part.description: An extrusion of a plan outline, or a sweep of a profile along a path. A void cuts what it meets (a firebox in a chimney, a hole through a slab) instead of being solid.

base.description: An extrusion's bottom above the level.

plane.description: An extrusion drawn on a face: its outline lies on this plane, and `base` and `height` run along the plane's normal (`x` × `y`).

profile.description: A sweep's section: `x` across the path (positive to its left), `y` up from it.

path.description: A sweep's path through points, `z` above the level.

closed.description: The path runs from its last point back to its first.

face_normal.description: A path drawn on a face: the face's outward normal, which the profile's `y` runs along instead of up.

wall.description: A sweep along a wall's id, at its top or base: it follows the wall (a coping, a plinth).

offset.description: Lifts a wall path off its edge.

extend.description: Runs a wall path on past the wall's start and end.

ifc_class.description: The IFC class it exports as.

Plane.description: A plane anywhere in the model: its origin (height above the level) and two square unit axes along it.

SiteElement.description: A site element: terrain, a hard landscape area, an earthwork (a pad, a pit or a trench) or a plant.

top.description: Terrain and area: the top above the level.

points.description: Terrain: spot heights `[x, y, z]`, `z` above the level.

contour.description: Terrain: a contour every so much height; 0 draws none.

lines.description: Terrain: the contours and break lines it passes through.

survey.description: Terrain: a survey, its edge takes its height from the data nearest it (else the edge stays at `top`).

faceted.description: Terrain: drawn as flat triangles between its points, not smoothed through them.

major.description: Terrain: every so many contours one is heavier; 0 is every fifth.

labels.description: Terrain: heavier contours carry their height.

levels.description: Terrain: spot heights carry their height.

shift.description: Terrain: what was taken off a survey's coordinates when it was brought in, metres: a survey point is its place here plus this.

pads.description: Terrain: the pads worked into the ground, in order.

under_buildings.description: Terrain: the ground is dug out under the slabs standing on it.

strata.description: Terrain: the soil under it, layer by layer from the top.

analysis.description: Terrain: shaded in plans by slope, aspect or height.

flow.description: Terrain: arrows in plans for which way water runs.

base.description: A plant's base above the level.

cut.description: A pad, pit or trench: its bank where it digs in, run over rise.

fill.description: A pad: its bank where it is made up, run over rise.

depth.description: A pit or a trench (kind `pad`): how deep below the ground; 0 is a pad at `top`.

width.description: A trench (kind `pad`): its width; its line is `path`.

only_cut.description: A pad that only digs: lower ground under it stays.

retained.description: A pad or a pit (kind `pad`): the edges cut upright whatever its banks, edge 0 from the first corner of `outline` to the second. A retaining wall standing on one is a wall element of its own, and is not tied to it here.

radius.description: A trench (kind `pad`): its bends rounded to this radius.

edges.description: A property: what each edge of its outline is, edge `i` from corner `i` to the next (the first front, on four sides the third rear, the rest sides when left out).

rules.description: A property: the planning rules it is built to.

path.description: A road: its centreline, `[x, y, z]` points, `z` its crown's level above the level there.

road.description: A road: its section and how it meets the ground.

drain.description: A drain: its run, pipe and fall.

tank.description: A tank: what it is and its size; it stands at `at`.

walk.description: A path: its line, width and surface.

investigation.description: A borehole, trial pit or probe: its log; it stands at `at`.

GroundLine.description: A line a terrain passes through: `[x, y, z]` points, `z` above the level. A contour has one height; a `sharp` line is a break line (a kerb, a bank top) the ground folds along.

GroundPad.description: A levelled platform worked into a terrain (or, with a `depth`, a pit or trench dug into it): its outline, its `level` above the terrain's level, and its banks, each the run for one unit of height (`cut` where it is dug in, `fill` where it is made up; 0 is an upright face).

depth.description: An excavation: above 0, the floor is this far below the ground all over (a pit, a trench) and `level` is not used.

SoilLayer.description: A layer of soil under a terrain, from the ground as surveyed down.

GroundShading.description: How a terrain is shaded in plans.

SitePattern.description: An area's surface: units (`size`, `stagger`, `angle`), lines (`spacing`, `angle`) or stipple (`spacing`).

LotEdge.description: What an edge of a property is: it sets the edge's setback.

LotRules.description: A property's planning rules, metres; a limit of 0 is none.

height.description: The highest the building may reach above the project's zero.

coverage.description: How much of the lot may be covered, 0 to 1.

floor_ratio.description: Floor area allowed per unit of lot area.

bearings.description: Bearings and lengths written along the edges in plans.

setbacks.description: Setback lines and the buildable area drawn in plans.

angle.description: Angle planes: degrees from the horizontal, rising inward from `angle_from` above each edge with a setback; 0 is none.

easements.description: Strips along edges kept clear of building.

own.description: Edges with a setback or a note of their own.

LotEasement.description: A strip `width` wide inside the lot along edge `edge` (0 is the first), kept clear of building.

LotEdgeRule.description: What edge `edge` of a lot (0 is the first) has of its own: a `setback` other than its kind's, and a `note` written on its setback line below its kind's setback, `note_offset` from there where it was dragged.

SiteRoad.description: A road's section, metres: the carriageway kerb to kerb, its fall across (per cent) from its crown or one way to its right, kerbs, footpaths each side, its make-up's depth, its banks into the ground (run for each metre of height) and its parking bays.

works.description: Worked into the terrain under it.

gullies.description: Gullies along its low edges this far apart, with a channel by the kerb; 0 is none.

radius.description: Its bends rounded to this radius on the centreline; 0 leaves them sharp.

RoadParking.description: Parking bays along a road's kerb: `width` along it (square to the bay), `length` out, at `angle` degrees to it (90 square on, 0 parallel).

ParkingSide.description: Which side of a road, looking along it.

SiteDrain.description: A drain run, metres: `path` in plan from its head down to its outfall, a pipe `diameter` across laid at `fall` per cent (1.25 is 1 in 80), its invert `depth` under the ground at its head, with a chamber `chamber` square inside at each point, in a trench `trench` wide on a bed `bed` deep.

SiteTank.description: A buried tank, metres: `length` by `width` inside, `depth` deep, turned `angle` degrees anticlockwise, its top `cover` under the ground, its walls `wall` thick, dug in with `working` room round it.

SitePath.description: A path on the ground, metres: along `path` in plan, `width` wide between its edging, following the ground, its surface and sub-base `thickness` deep, with `edging` this wide each side (0 for none).

radius.description: Its bends rounded to this radius; 0 leaves them sharp.

SiteProbe.description: A borehole, trial pit or probe of a soils report, as the report logs it: depths below its own ground level, `ground` that level above the level's datum as the report gives it (left out, the existing ground's height there).

layers.description: Its layers from the top down, each to the depth of its foot.

ProbeLayer.description: A layer of a log: from the foot of the one above down to `to`.

unit.description: The report's name for it across the site: "GT3".

SoilType.description: The soil family a layer is drawn with.

ProbeWater.description: Water struck at `depth`, rising to `rest` if the report says.

ProbeTest.description: A test at `depth` and its result; `text` as the report writes it when the number alone doesn't say it all ("50/220 mm").

Object.description: Furniture or a fixture from CreaBIM's catalogue.

catalogue.description: The catalogue object's key: "starter/sofa-3" (`creabim catalogue` lists them; "starter/" may be left out).

at.description: Where it goes in plan: its origin (the middle of its back edge), or its middle with `anchor` "centre".

rotation.description: Turn, degrees anticlockwise. At 0 its back is towards +y.

offset.description: Its floor above the level (for one hung from the ceiling, its top below the ceiling). Left out: the catalogue's.

light.description: The light it gives in a render, when not its kind's usual one. It belongs to the object's type: every object of the same `catalogue` key shares it, so state it the same on each (or on one; the last stated is kept).

Anchor.description: Which point of an object `at` gives.

ObjectLight.description: The light a fitting gives in a render.

on.description: False: it is drawn, and gives no light.

lumens.description: Its output, lumens: about 800 for a 60 W bulb of old.

kelvin.description: Its colour, kelvin: 2700 warm, 4000 neutral, 6500 daylight.

group.description: The group it is dimmed with in Visuals; left out, its type's name.

Room.description: A room: the space the walls close off round `at`, or an outline drawn for it.

at.description: A point inside it, where its tag sits.

outline.description: An outline of its own; left out, the walls round `at` bound it.

height.description: Its top above its level. Left out: to the ceiling, or the level's height.

View.description: A view: a plan of a level, a section or elevation along a line, a 3D view, or a schedule. Which fields it uses depends on its `kind`: plan: `level`, `cut_height`, `ceiling_plan`; section and elevation: `start`, `end`, `depth`; 3d: `azimuth`, `altitude`; schedule: `category`, `by_type`.

name.description: Its title; the id when left out.

style.description: Left out: shaded for 3D views, hidden line for the rest.

cut_height.description: A plan's cut above its level.

room_colours.description: Each room washed in a colour of its own.

start.description: A section or elevation's line. It looks to the left of start → end: a line drawn west to east looks north.

depth.description: How far a section or elevation looks.

azimuth.description: A 3D view's compass bearing: 0 from the south, anticlockwise.

altitude.description: A 3D view's angle above the horizon.

drain.description: A long section: the drain it follows.

probe.description: A borehole log: the borehole, trial pit or probe it logs.

stair.description: A walk-line section: the stair it unrolls.

by_type.description: A schedule's rows grouped by type.

callout.description: Makes it a callout of another view: an enlarged part of it. Give it the same kind and line (or level) as its parent.

site.description: A plan, section, elevation or 3D view: how it shows the site.

Callout.description: The box of a parent view a callout enlarges, in that view's drawing coordinates.

ViewSite.description: How a view shows the site: the ground before or after its works (or after with the ground as it was dashed), and each kind of site information on or off.

limit.description: The line round what the works change.

Sheet.description: A drawing sheet, with views placed on it. Its id is its number.

name.description: Its title; the number when left out.

size.description: An ISO paper size, landscape. Give this or `width` and `height`.

Viewport.description: A view placed on a sheet.

at.description: Where on the sheet, in millimetres from its lower left corner.

target.description: The drawing point (in the file's units, as the drawing's x and y) put at `at`. Left out: the middle of the crop, or of the whole drawing.

crop.description: Only this part of the drawing is shown (drawing coordinates).

fit.description: A stair's id: the crop follows that stair, its footprint with a margin round it, as it moves or grows; `crop` is used once it is gone.

Tag.description: A tag in a view, showing an element's mark (a door's, a window's) or a room's name, number and area. It moves with its element.

element.description: The id of the element it tags.

offset.description: Where it sits, from the element's middle, in drawing units.

elbow.description: A bend in its leader, from the element's middle.

end.description: Where its leader ends, from the element's middle; left out, at the middle.

Note.description: Text in a view (drawing coordinates, in the file's units) or on a sheet (paper millimetres).

view.description: A view's id, or a sheet's.

at.description: Where its first line starts: its left end, mid-height.

leader.description: A leader from the text to this point, in the same units as `at`.

symbol.description: Drawn as a CreaBIM symbol instead of as text, `text` going in the symbol's slot when it has one.

NoteSymbol.description: A symbol placed with the Symbol tool, its middle on the note's `at`.

style.description: A style of that kind, as `slopes.ramp_rise_arrow`; left out, the kind's pick in the project's style pack.
